name: Battle of Brémule and Anglo-Norman Stability
summary: Henry I of England defeats Louis VI of France at Brémule, securing Normandy against French pressure. The battle demonstrates the Anglo-Norman dual monarchy's military capacity. Henry's subsequent loss of his heir in the White Ship disaster (1120) triggers the Anarchy succession crisis.

_quarry.structural_significance: Consolidates Anglo-Norman control of northern France; the White Ship disaster destabilizes the succession and leads to civil war, demonstrating how personal dynasticism shapes medieval political stability.
